newsitem.title: FRANCE: French railways SNCF aims for breakeven in 1999.
newsitem.headline: French railways SNCF aims for breakeven in 1999.

text.p: French state-owned railways SNCF, which lost 15.2 billion francs ($2.7 billion) in 1996, said it expected to lose around two billion francs this year but aims to break even in 1999.

After a staff council meeting on Wednesday, the SNCF said the 1997 budget took into account the creation of the RFF (Reseau Ferre de France) entity which will take up 134.2 billion francs of debt, reducing SNCF's financial expenses by around eight billion francs annually.

"This measure allows the railway to provisionally estimate a two billion franc loss for 1997 with prospects for a return to breakeven in 1999," the SNCF said in a statement. It assumed an average tariff increase of 0.5 percent which, however, represented a drop in constant francs, it said.
